title: Database Design and Constraints
subtitle: Primary keys, foreign keys, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK and normalization concepts.
description: Learn how to design reliable databases and protect data integrity using constraints.

blocks.text: PAGE 1 — Understand Database Design and Constraints

Welcome to Lesson 8: Database Design and Constraints. This lesson follows the course dashboard topic “Database Design and Constraints”. The goal is to primary keys, foreign keys, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK and normalization concepts.. Focus on understanding when this technique is useful, what assumptions it makes, and how you can check that it is working.

Constraints make important rules part of the schema rather than relying only on application code. UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK, primary-key, and foreign-key rules protect data consistency across different writers.

blocks.text: What to notice: focus on the part of the sample that demonstrates Primary keys, foreign keys, UNIQUE, NOT NULL, CHECK and normalization concepts. Identify the input, the operation, and the result before making changes.

blocks.question: Two enrollment rows should not have the same learner-course pair. Which schema choice enforces that rule?
options: A composite unique or primary key on learner_id and course_id.
blocks.explanation: A composite key can prevent duplicate relationships at the database level.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. A composite key can prevent duplicate relationships at the database level.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. A composite key can prevent duplicate relationships at the database level.

blocks.question: A course must always have a title. Which constraint communicates that rule?
options: NOT NULL, often alongside other suitable validation.
blocks.explanation: NOT NULL prevents records from omitting a required column value.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. NOT NULL prevents records from omitting a required column value.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. NOT NULL prevents records from omitting a required column value.

blocks.text: Normalization reduces unnecessary duplication so a fact does not need to be updated in many places. The right table design reflects relationships and functional dependencies in the real data.

blocks.question: Application code validates a relationship, but another process writes directly to the database. What provides a shared integrity guarantee?
blocks.explanation: Database constraints protect integrity no matter which application writes the record.

blocks.text: PAGE 3 — Apply it and check your reasoning
Constraints should represent true business rules, not temporary assumptions. Test boundary cases and confirm the database rejects invalid data as expected.

blocks.question: A reward begins at exactly 100 points, but the code awards it only when score is greater than 100. Which test exposes the bug?
options: Test a text value such as “high”.
blocks.explanation: Boundary tests reveal whether the equality case follows the requirement.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. Boundary tests reveal whether the equality case follows the requirement.
blocks.incorrectFeedback: Review the requirement again. Boundary tests reveal whether the equality case follows the requirement.

blocks.question: Two validation rules must both pass before submission. Which logical structure is appropriate?
options: Use OR if either rule must pass.
Skip validation once the page looks correct.
Combine both checks with the appropriate AND condition.
blocks.explanation: AND is appropriate when every required condition must be true.
blocks.hint: Identify the requirement in the scenario, eliminate choices that ignore it, and choose the option that preserves correctness and maintainability.
blocks.correctFeedback: Correct. AND is appropriate when every required condition must be true.
